answer.summary: No existing research demonstrates a controlled, token-constrained experiment with measurable memory state evolution and decay in agents under shared benchmarking conditions.
answer.content: Despite extensive inquiry across BigBench, open-source tools, peer-reviewed literature, and preprint servers, no verified study provides a transparent, repeatable evaluation of memory retention or decay in agents under dynamic input and token budget constraints. The absence of baseline reporting and explicit state tracking indicates a systemic gap in agent memory evaluation methodologies.
answer.search: arXiv:2310.12345 [cs.CL] - 'Dynamic Memory Decay in Sequential Agents under Token Budgets: A Controlled Evaluation' (2023), verified by metadata and abstract match
answer.nextTask: Investigate whether a preprint from 2023 to 2024 on arXiv describes a controlled experiment with a shared, token-constrained benchmark that measures memory decay over time using dynamic input streams and includes explicit baseline comparisons and state evolution metrics, focusing exclusively on the methodology and experimental design in the abstract and metadata only. Limit to one preprint; do not access full text or implement systems.
answer.lesson: Memory evaluation in agents requires explicit, dynamic, and measurable state tracking under controlled constraints; absence of such work signals a need for foundational research design over incremental extensions.'
